title: Rivergate and Landfall
premise: Sable Sterling has spent a decade outrunning his father's legacy — and the Rivergate expedition that killed him and ruined three reputations. When old rival Marguerite Voss offers the crew a fortune to salvage the wreck of the Landfall, the very ship Sable's father died chasing, he refuses — until her salvage fleet's backers turn out to be the same syndicate that falsified the original expedition's records and let his father take the blame. Racing the syndicate's armed fleet and a six-tide window before the channel silts shut, Sable dives the Landfall and finds not treasure but his father's field journal, proving the syndicate sank the ship deliberately to bury a fraud. In the climax, Sable chooses truth over the salvage fortune, broadcasting the journal and surrendering the wreck to maritime authorities, and finally stops running — inheriting not his father's shame but his unfinished work.
about_author: Yara Almeida is a former maritime surveyor who spent five years mapping wreck sites off the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who are better at leaving than at staying.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Sable Sterling's POV. Working a black-market dig in a coastal boomtown, Sable wraps a job, takes his pay, and is gone before dawn — a ritual the reader learns he has performed for ten years. A postcard from a dead man's handwriting unsettles him. Emotional beat: restless competence masking grief he won't name.

chapters.title: Marguerite Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Voss, his father's old rival, finds him in a dockside bar with a contract: salvage the Landfall before her backers' fleet does. Sable refuses flatly and walks out. Emotional beat: old resentment flaring into something colder — fear of what the wreck actually holds.

chapters.title: The Crew That Keeps Choosing Him
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. His small crew — engineer Dessa, diver Okafor, and teenage deckhand Pip — vote to take Voss's job over his objection, needing the money and, they admit, needing Sable to stop running. Emotional beat: loyalty as a claim on him he can't dodge.

chapters.title: What the Rivergate Files Say
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. Dessa digs through leaked expedition records and finds the official Rivergate report is doctored: tide logs altered, a diver's name erased. She shows Sable, who recognizes his father's notation style in the margins. Emotional beat: the past is not finished with him.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A harbor pilot explains the channel to the wreck site silts shut after the spring tides — a six-tide window for everyone. The syndicate's salvage fleet is already underway. Emotional beat: the race becomes real, and Sable commits for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Out Past the Buoys
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The crew's patched-together boat makes open water; Okafor reads the crew's fractures — Pip hero-worships Sable, Dessa distrusts Voss, Sable trusts no one. First shadowing contact from the syndicate fleet. Emotional beat: camaraderie forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Voss's Version of the Truth
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss reveals she was on Rivergate as a young diver, that she saw something she's kept silent about for a decade, and that the syndicate owns her debts. She isn't after treasure; she's after absolution. Emotional beat: the rival becomes a mirror.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Outer Shelf
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. First dive on the wreck site — wrong coordinates, deliberately corrupted charts. Sable reads the seabed like his father taught him and finds the true scatter field. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into skill; the inheritance he can't refuse.

chapters.title: Pip Overboard
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip disobeys orders to retrieve a loose artifact and is caught in a surge; Sable goes in after him and both barely surface. Sable's fury and terror crack his detachment open. Emotional beat: he realizes he has people to lose again.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. A syndicate launch delivers an offer: walk away rich, or the fleet will take the site and the crew's records — including Sable's forged permits. Justice outside the law cuts both ways. Emotional beat: the moral ground shifts under everyone.

chapters.title: Second and Third Tides
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Grinding salvage montage: hull breach, silt, a locked strongroom they can't crack before dark. The syndicate fleet anchors within sight, patient as weather. Emotional beat: fatigue, friction, and the strange peace of shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Strongroom Opens
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Inside: not bullion but sealed documents and a waterproof field journal in his father's hand. Sable reads the first pages alone at night and learns Rivergate's cargo manifest was falsified before the ship ever sank. Emotional beat: vertigo — his whole life was built on a lie.

chapters.title: What My Father Was Building
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The journal, continued: his father wasn't salvaging the Landfall; he was documenting the syndicate's insurance fraud and planned to testify. He died — or was made to die — before he could. Emotional beat: rage arriving where grief had been.

chapters.title: Voss Breaks
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Sable confronts Voss; she confesses she was paid to alter the tide logs and has hated herself for ten years. She gives him the one document that corroborates the journal — her original dive log. Emotional beat: confession as the beginning of loyalty.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Fleet Moves
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. The syndicate, tipped off by a bought crew member, raids the site at slack water. In the chaos the journal is nearly lost; Pip saves it and is injured. The traitor is exposed. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the family of the boat.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Choice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cornered, the syndicate offers Sable everything: his father's name cleared quietly, the salvage fortune, silence about the fraud. He can have justice or the truth, not both. Emotional beat: the temptation of a clean, dishonest ending.

chapters.title: Storm Glass
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. A squall line closes the channel early; the final tide window shrinks to hours. The crew votes — not to run, but to finish the job Sable's father started. Emotional beat: the crew chooses him back, and he lets them.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Last Dive
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable makes the final dive alone into the flooded strongroom as the syndicate closes in above. He recovers the complete evidence cache as the channel begins to choke with silt. Emotional beat: descending into his father's last minutes, and surfacing changed.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dessa's POV. Rather than sell the evidence, the crew transmits the journal, Voss's log, and the manifest to maritime authorities, press, and every port on the coast before the syndicate can jam them. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon that can't be repossessed.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The syndicate fleet is impounded at anchor; its backers scatter. Voss surrenders to the investigators, asking Sable to tell her father's story straight. Sable stands on the quarterdeck of the boat he nearly lost and does not leave. Emotional beat: stillness, earned.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At a small hearing, the Rivergate verdict is overturned and his father's name restored. Sable donates the Landfall's recovered papers to the maritime archive and takes a legitimate survey contract — with his crew, on his terms. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Weeks later, Pip watches Sable sleep in past dawn for the first time — the man who always left, staying. A new postcard arrives with the dead man's handwriting: his father's last letter, finally delivered. Sable reads it, smiles, and stays for breakfast. Emotional beat: quiet, complete arrival.
